content.text: Two people might do the same amount of work, but one might do it faster than the other. The person who does it faster has more power. Power tells us the rate at which energy is transferred or work is done.
Power is the rate of energy transfer. It is measured in watts (W), where 1 watt = 1 joule per second. A more powerful device transfers the same amount of energy in less time.
is the rate of energy transfer, or the rate of doing work.
Measures how quickly energy is transferred
A more powerful device transfers energy faster
If two machines do the same work:
The one that does it in less time has more power
If two machines have the same power:
In the same time, they transfer the same energy
The one running longer transfers more energy total
One watt equals one joule per second.
Power in Terms of Force and Velocity
This is useful for moving vehicles.
A machine does 600 J of work in 20 seconds. Calculate its power.
A 2 kW heater runs for 5 minutes. How much energy does it transfer?
A motor lifts a 50 kg mass through 8 m in 4 seconds. Calculate the power. (g = 10 N/kg)
Work done = GPE gained = mgh = 50 × 10 × 8 = 4000 J
A car engine provides 15 kW of power. The car travels at a constant 25 m/s on a level road. What is the resistive force?
At constant velocity, driving force = resistive force.
A cyclist provides 400 W of power. Against a total resistance of 50 N, what constant speed can they maintain?
Two lifts raise the same load 20 m. Lift A takes 10 s, lift B takes 25 s. Compare their powers.
Both do the same work (W), but in different times.
Lift A has 2.5 times the power of lift B.

Remember that P = Fv only works when the force and velocity are in the same direction and the object is moving at constant velocity. Convert all units to SI before calculating.
Car engines are rated in kW (or horsepower)
Higher power = faster acceleration (for same mass)
Power determines top speed (when P = Fv at maximum v)
Electricity is charged by energy used (kWh), not power
A 2 kW heater running for 3 hours uses 6 kWh
Power tells you the rate; time determines total energy
is the energy used by a 1 kW device in 1 hour.
The kilowatt-hour (kWh) is a unit of energy, not power. 1 kWh = 3,600,000 J. It is the energy transferred by a 1 kW device running for 1 hour.
— Power is the RATE of energy transfer. Energy is the total amount transferred.
— Only if running for the same time. A 3 kW kettle for 2 minutes uses less energy than a 100 W lamp for 24 hours.
— Watts measure power (J/s). Joules measure energy. They're related but different.
— High power means fast energy transfer, but also means higher energy bills if used longer.
— Due to inefficiency, power output is always less than power input.
